newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia shares tumble, no pick-up seen near term.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia shares tumble, no pick-up seen near term.

text.p: Slovenian shares fell 1.73 percent on Tuesday and traders said a revival in the bourse's fortunes could not be expected until after April when banks open first custodian accounts for international investors.
"The return of foreign investors is expected to bring expectations of better liquidity and higher prices, even if volumes do not increase significantly as early as in April," one trader said.

The Bank of Slovenian five weeks ago blocked foreign buying by saying international investors must open custodian accounts at Slovenian banks in order to be able to trade in Slovenian shares. Since then the index has fallen 19.2 percent.
"In the next two weeks I cannot see a rise in the price of any share on the market, except for possible short-term rises," said Davor Dubokovic, a trader of brokerage Eastbrokers.

"If foreigners fail to begin buying Slovenian shares again due to 12 percent costs of new accounts or to disappointment over the unexpected central bank decree, prices may continue falling for months," one analyst said.
The SBI index fell 23.56 points to 1,338.26.
Issue A of drug company Lek was most actively traded, easing 0.26 percent to 26,590 tolars on volume of 783 shares.
Overall 11 shares fell, four rose and 11 were untraded. Turnover fell to 64 million tolars from 126.7 million.
Financial consultancy Primofin was the leading decliner, down 10.69 percent to 14,200 tolars on volume of 24 shares.
Ordinary shares of trader Kovinotehna were the top gainers, rising 2.6 percent to 473 on volume of 966 shares.
